title: Hexagons, Salar de Uyuni, Bolivia (2086104060).jpg
author: Pedro Szekely from Los Angeles, USA
description: The ridges form as the salt crystallises from the evaporating water following the rains each year. Salar de Uyuni (or Salar de Tunupa) is the world's largest salt flat at 10,582 km² (4,085 square miles)[1].
